paper.title: SA-LUT: Spatial Adaptive 4D Look-Up Table for Photorealistic Style Transfer

method.inference_predictor: style/content encoder predicts a 64-way simplex weight vector and a one-channel spatial context map
method.explicit_operator: identity-residual 4D LUT with two context bins and 17x17x17 RGB nodes
method.renderer: quadrilinear interpolation over context plus RGB, followed by output save clipping
method.spatial_parameter: network-predicted context map resized bilinearly to output resolution
method.synthetic_training: professional 3D LUTs applied to Log-space image pairs
method.real_style_training: frozen direct Style2Log image-to-image network supplies pseudo Log content and a learned discriminator supplies adversarial style supervision

pst50.role: photorealistic style-transfer benchmark, not film-stock training truth

reopen_condition: a clean-room, non-adversarial, no-direct-image-generator training design plus rights-cleared manifest-complete supervision and a separately frozen question that passes stock/data identifiability gates
forbidden_rescues: download or run the official checkpoint while treating its output as non-generative project evidence
treat PST50 styles or ground truth as film-stock truth
use the context map as an unconstrained semantic mask in Style-safe production
train on current closed Commons/YFCC pixels
infer an operator from unrelated style photographs
copy the non-commercial implementation into production
omit the undeclared image, LUT or Style2Log checkpoint lineage
present node clamping or monotonicity loss as a severe-artifact guarantee
claim_ceiling: current primary-source source/method/training-boundary audit: SA-LUT demonstrates a useful explicit 4D-LUT plus spatial-context architecture, but its official checkpoint is trained with a direct pseudo-Log image generator and adversarial supervision under incomplete asset lineage; it provides no film-stock or unpaired-operator evidence and is not executed
